questions.q: In the capstone's classification tool output, what is the purpose of the "proposedAction" field?
options: It is a cosmetic label with no effect on the flow's behavior
It determines whether the ticket can be routed automatically or must wait for human approval before anything happens
It records which employee originally submitted the support ticket
It sets the font color used in the support team's Teams channel
questions.explain: proposedAction is the hinge the whole system turns on: a value like "route" allows automatic handling, while "escalate" or "close" routes the ticket into the human approval gate instead.

questions.q: Why is the classification tool built as a separate flow from the approval flow, rather than one combined flow?
options: Because Copilot Studio limits every flow to a single action
Because the classification tool must respond to the agent synchronously within about 100 seconds, while a human approval can take much longer and must live in a separately triggered flow
Because combined flows are not supported by the Approvals connector
There is no real reason; it was an arbitrary design choice
questions.explain: This follows directly from Lesson 18's two-flow pattern: the agent-called tool flow must respond fast and synchronously, so the slower, human-paced approval step has to live in its own independently triggered flow.

questions.q: What happens if a support lead rejects an approval request for a ticket flagged to auto-escalate?
options: The ticket is permanently deleted
The ticket is escalated anyway, overriding the rejection
The ticket falls back to the default human-review queue instead of being auto-escalated
The agent is automatically disabled for all future tickets
questions.explain: A rejection routes the ticket to the default human-review queue rather than letting the proposed action happen — the whole point of the gate is that nothing irreversible runs without a person agreeing first.

questions.q: Which approval type does the capstone use for the escalate/close approval gate, and why?
options: Everyone must approve, because every support lead needs to weigh in on every ticket
First to respond, so any one support lead can clear routine escalations or closures quickly
Sequential approval through the entire company leadership chain
No approval type is specified; it is left undefined
questions.explain: The capstone uses "First to respond" so that any one member of the support lead team can clear the approval quickly, rather than requiring a slower, stricter unanimous or sequential process for routine ticket actions.

questions.q: What happens to a ticket that doesn't clearly match any of the automated routing categories?
options: It is discarded without any record
It is automatically closed as unresolved
It falls to a default human-review queue
The agent repeatedly asks the customer to resubmit until it matches a category
questions.explain: Anything that doesn't fit cleanly into Dispatch, Billing, Claims, or Security/IT falls to a default human-review queue, ensuring ambiguous tickets still get a person's attention rather than being mishandled.
